- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to revert — cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 3–5% of spike magnitude.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model often overestimates mean reversion — reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with observed mean decay.  
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > +0.3), model tends to overreact — cap forecast increase at 1.2x recent high or apply downward drag of 3–5% to prevent runaway growth.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates downward trends in sentiment-heavy periods — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment average < -0.3 over last 7 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings > ±0.3 per day), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values before projecting.
